hpi_details: A 20-year-old female presents to the clinic with bilateral band-like squeezing pressure headache. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks staring at computer screens late into the night while studying for university exams has severely strained her neck and eyes.
concerns: She is worried the constant squeezing pain will prevent her from studying and cause her to fail her university final exams next week.
expectations: She hopes to get a strong prescription painkiller and a medical excuse note for her university professors.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Tension Headache is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Tension Headache: Acetaminophen, NSAIDs, posture check, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: bilateral band-like squeezing pressure headache

Key HPI features: A 20-year-old female presents to the clinic with bilateral band-like squeezing pressure headache. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Tension Headache.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Tension Headache.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Migraine without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

Ignoring critical warning signs such as: sudden severe 'thunderclap' onset, new or worsening headache with fever, neck stiffness, focal neurological signs, new headache after age 50, or headache waking the patient from sleep/worse in the morning.
management_principles: Plan for Tension Headache: Acetaminophen, NSAIDs, posture check
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of bilateral band-like squeezing pressure headache. HPI: stress, poor posture, lack of sleep.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Tension Headache.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Tension Headache.
reference_soap.plan: Plan for Tension Headache: Acetaminophen, NSAIDs, posture check. Consult specialist if symptoms worsen. Counsel patient.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Tension Headache
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Tension Headache
Implement evidence-based management plan: Acetaminophen, NSAIDs, posture check

teaching.one_liner: A bilateral, band-like pressure headache from stress, poor posture, or lack of sleep — the most common type of headache, without the throbbing or nausea seen in migraine.
red_flags: Sudden severe 'thunderclap' onset — must exclude subarachnoid haemorrhage
New or worsening headache with fever, neck stiffness, or focal neurological signs — raises concern for meningitis or a structural lesion
New headache after age 50, or headache waking the patient from sleep/worse in the morning — warrants imaging to exclude a secondary cause

must_ask.say: Does it feel like a tight band around your head, on both sides?
Does stress, poor sleep, or posture seem to bring this on?
Any nausea, vomiting, or light sensitivity?
How often do these happen, and how long do they last?
How often are you taking pain relievers for this?

history.answer: I've had this constant dull, squeezing headache that feels like a tight band around my head, and I've been feeling really tired.
It started about two weeks ago and has been building up gradually, getting steadily worse rather than hitting me all at once.
I've occasionally had mild headaches before when I was tired, but nothing that lingered like this or felt this constant.
It hurts on both sides across my forehead, around both temples, and extends all the way around to the back of my head.
It feels like a steady squeezing pressure or a tight vise gripping my head, about a four or five out of ten in pain.
The ache is present for most of the day, but it tends to get noticeably worse in the late afternoon and evening after studying.
Sitting at my desk with poor posture makes it tighter, but walking or normal movement doesn't make it worse; resting in a quiet room helps a little.
No, I haven't seen any flashing lights, blind spots, or zigzags before or during the headache.
No, my stomach feels completely fine with no nausea or vomiting, and bright lights or normal sounds don't bother me.
No, my eyes don't tear up or get red, my nose isn't congested or runny, and my eyelids aren't drooping.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or stiff neck at all.
No, I haven't had any weakness, numbness, tingling, slurred speech, confusion, or seizures.
No, my vision is completely normal with no blurriness, double vision, or pain behind my eyes.
No, I haven't bumped my head or had any head injuries recently.
I haven't taken any painkillers or other medicines for this headache; I've just been trying to rest.
I've been under a lot of stress with college exams lately, studying long hours hunched over my desk, and barely sleeping five hours a night.
No, I've never had high blood pressure, and I don't take any blood pressure medication or blood thinners.
No, no one around me or in my dorm has a headache, and we don't have any gas or fuel-burning heaters.
No, I don't have cancer, HIV, or any conditions that weaken my immune system.
Yes, along with the headache, I've been feeling generalized fatigue and drained of energy over the past couple of weeks.
I don't have any chronic medical illnesses or conditions; I've always been healthy.
I've never had any operations, and I've never been admitted to a hospital.
I am not taking any prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, or herbal supplements.
No, I have no known allergies to any medications, foods, or other substances.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I only drink socially, maybe a glass of beer once or twice a month with friends.
I'm a sophomore in college studying long hours at a desk, and I currently live in a university dormitory.
No one in my family has a history of brain tumors, aneurysms, or chronic headache disorders.
My last period started about two weeks ago, and my menstrual cycles are regular every twenty-eight days.
There is no possibility of pregnancy, and I am not currently sexually active.
I thought maybe all the late-night cramming on my laptop under bright lights just gave me terrible eye and neck strain.
I'm really worried that this pressure in my head will keep me from focusing and make me fail my college finals next week.
I was hoping for a strong painkiller that actually works and a doctor's note I can give to my university professors.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 116/74 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6°C, SpO2 99% on room air.
Alert, fully oriented to person, place, and time, with clear, fluent speech and normal attention.
Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light; visual fields full to confrontation; fundoscopy shows sharp optic disc margins without papilledema or retinal hemorrhages.
Cranial nerves II through XII are intact; normal facial sensation and symmetric facial movements; intact extraocular motility without nystagmus.
Neck supple with full active and passive flexion; Kernig and Brudzinski signs are negative.
Motor strength is 5/5 in all four extremities; normal muscle bulk and tone bilaterally.
Intact sensation to light touch, pinprick, and proprioception symmetrically throughout the face, arms, and legs.
Biceps, patellar, and Achilles deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally; plantar responses are flexor bilaterally.
Finger-to-nose and rapid alternating movements are smooth and accurate; normal gait and negative Romberg sign.
No tenderness to palpation or percussion over the frontal or maxillary sinuses bilaterally.
Bilateral posterior paracervical and upper trapezius muscles are tender to palpation without cervical spine bony tenderness; neck range of motion is full.
